title: Fair Isle triangle shawl
subtitle: A top-down DK triangle with a stranded colourwork band at the centre back.
excerpt: A top-down triangular shawl in DK wool with a wide stranded Fair Isle band worked across the spine once the shawl is deep enough to hold a full peerie pattern. Garter stitch forms the body above and below the band. Wingspan 155 cm, centre-back depth 72 cm when blocked. About 250 g of main colour plus 80 g of contrast.
sourceNotes: Stranded colourwork in shawls is part of the Shetland and Fair Isle tradition. The 8-stitch peerie motif is a standard element in Shetland knitting documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Colour patterns, and in the Fair Isle Heritage Trust collection. Sharon Miller, Heirloom Knitting (2004), covers Shetland peerie patterns comprehensively; Miller's specific charts are not reproduced here.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 44 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan 155 cm. Centre-back depth 72 cm. Blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small stranded-colourwork motif of typically 6 to 12 stitches wide, used as a border or accent band between larger Fair Isle patterns. The word peerie is Shetland dialect for small.
A small strip of garter stitch worked on a few stitches, rotated and picked up to form the centre-back starting point of a top-down triangle shawl.

In stranded colourwork worked flat, the colour that is carried below the other in the right hand (or picked consistently from below in the left). The dominant colour sits slightly lower in the stitch and appears more prominent in the finished fabric. Consistency matters more than which colour is dominant.

content.text: A top-down DK triangle shawl with a wide
peerie pattern
Fair Isle band set into the centre of the body. Wings are plain garter above and below the band. Wingspan 155 cm, depth 72 cm.

The colourwork band sits roughly in the middle of the depth, worked flat across the full width once the shawl is about 35 cm deep. The band is 20 rows deep (5 peerie repeats of 4 rows). Above and below it, the shawl is plain garter stitch with the standard four-per-RS-row spine increases. Working the band flat rather than in the round means the WS rows are read in reverse; the motif chart must be read right to left on RS rows and left to right on WS rows. Assign the
dominant colour
before the first band row and keep it consistent throughout. Budget about 250 g of main colour (MC) and 80 g of contrast (CC) in DK wool.
What you need

items.name: Main colour (MC)
items.qty: About 250 g (550 m / 600 yards) of DK-weight yarn

items.name: Contrast colour (CC)
items.qty: About 80 g (175 m / 190 yards) of DK-weight yarn, strongly contrasting

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. Stranded colourwork typically runs about 1 to 2 stitches per 10 cm tighter than single-colour garter because the floats sit across the back. The band itself will be very slightly narrower than the garter sections, but since it is only 20 rows of a much longer piece, the visual effect is minimal. If your garter gauge is 24 stitches per 10 cm, the finished wingspan will be about 142 cm at the same row count.
Stitches used
Pattern
Garter tab cast-on and garter body
Work the
garter tab

in MC: 3 sts on waste yarn, 6 rows garter, pick up 9 sts, 3 markers. Work the standard top-down increase (4 sts per RS row) in garter stitch with MC until the centre-back depth reaches approximately 35 cm (approximately 77 RS rows at gauge, giving 9 + 308 = 317 sts).
Peerie band

Work 20 rows (5 complete 4-row peerie repeats) in stranded colourwork with MC and CC. On every RS row, continue the 4-stitch yo-increase at each marker position. The colourwork pattern for one 4-row peerie repeat (on each 8-stitch group):
Row 1 (RS): *k1 MC, k1 CC, k1 MC, k1 CC, k1 MC, k1 CC, k1 MC, k1 CC; repeat from *.
Row 2 (WS): *p1 CC, p1 MC, p1 CC, p1 MC, p1 CC, p1 MC, p1 CC, p1 MC; repeat from *.
Row 3 (RS): *k2 MC, k4 CC, k2 MC; repeat from *.
Row 4 (WS): *p2 CC, p4 MC, p2 CC; repeat from *.
Repeat these 4 rows 5 times total for the band. The stitch count grows by 4 sts on every RS row throughout the band section.
Garter body to cast-off
After the band, continue in MC garter stitch with the standard increases until the wingspan reaches 155 cm, then bind off.
Stitch count check-ins
At the start of the peerie band (approximately 77 RS rows): 317 stitches. Check both wings are balanced before starting the colourwork.
At cast-off (approximately 170 RS rows): 9 + 680 = 689 stitches.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off in MC. A standard bind-off restricts the wingspan.
Common faults

Floats too tight on the WS: the CC strand was pulled hard between MC stitches rather than spread across the needle width. Spread the stitches on the needle before catching the CC float so the float length matches the stitch spread.

Dominant colour switching mid-row: the two yarns were swapped in the carrying hand mid-row. Decide which colour is dominant before the first band row and keep the same yarn in the same hand throughout all 20 band rows.
Band puckered after blocking: the colourwork tension ran 2 or more stitches per 10 cm tighter than the garter gauge. Work the colourwork band on needles one size larger than the garter body.
Blocking

Wet-block to wingspan 155 cm and depth 72 cm. The colourwork band will become slightly more supple after blocking. Check the colour does not bleed before blocking: soak a small swatch of the CC yarn in cold water and press on a white cloth.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Wash gently to avoid agitating the WS floats into matting. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

A traditional Shetland shawl body uses multiple peerie bands alternated with plain garter sections. Moving from a single band to a sequence of three or five bands with plain sections between them gives a more Shetland-traditional density of colourwork.
